added_failures_note: The reviewed run is a read-only map node: its manifest carries no suite arm (baseline_suite and after_suite are empty because no pytest suite ran and no code moved). added_failure_count is therefore derived as 0 with added_failure_ids [] from the absence of any suite arm, not from a suite delta. The node's own gate is check_map.py, whose positive arm is map-gate.log (EXIT=0) and negative arm is map-negative.log (EXIT=1). I independently reproduced both at head f55383af: rerunning check_map.py against the committed map prints base_statement_count=396 placed_count=396 expected_names=396, max_estimated_tokens=34535, module_level_edges=0, EXIT=0; deleting a member from a scratch copy prints placed_count=395, missing={'_LAUNCHED_WORKERS':1}, EXIT=1.

findings.text: the fragment reports 396 statements placed and 153,299 base tokens but does not reconcile these with §3's own figure 'the module's 320 top-level definitions'. Independent count at base d01750d78: 396 non-import top-level statements = 309 functions + 12 classes (321 definitions) + 74 assignments + 1 __main__ guard. The map's scope (all statements) is the brief's, and is the correct one for a pure move, but the plan's '320 definitions' figure is stale against the base and a reader comparing map to plan sees an apparent 76-statement gap. Recommend the coordinator refresh §3's count when recording the outcome.

the size estimate is re-derived as a literal math.ceil(bytes / 3.5) in the builder and the checker rather than calling reckon.crew.routing._tokens_for_bytes, which the brief names as the definition of the measure. The two are numerically identical (_tokens_for_bytes is math.ceil(max(0, byte_count)/3.5)) and every recomputed figure matches, so no value is wrong; this is a reuse nit only, and the checker's independent re-derivation of each estimate from the AST is what makes the map trustworthy.

justifications.durability: Both deliverables are committed locally in two focused commits each carrying a subject and a body, and the run directory holds the builder, the two gate logs and the negative-control log on a durable path. The map JSON carries its own base sha and a commands list so a later reader can rerun the census. Held off a full 20 because the checker itself (check_map.py) lives only in the run directory and not in the repo, so reproducing the map's verification requires the run-directory path; the brief assigned scripts/check_pure_move.py to a separate guard node, so this is expected for this node rather than a defect.
justifications.evidence: The evidence is strong and independently reproduced. The positive gate check_map.py at head f55383af exits 0 (396/396, max 34535, 0 module-level edges, census 182 imports/82 patches/2 source_reads/7 module_state), reproduced by me from the committed map. The negative control is genuinely falsifiable: I removed a different member (_LAUNCHED_WORKERS) than the manifest's (DONE_WHEN_PLAN_TEXT_SPAN_WORDS) from a scratch copy and the checker reported missing={'_LAUNCHED_WORKERS':1}, EXIT=1 - so the checker is not fail-open and its failure does not depend on the one member the manifest chose. Census spot-checks pass: 'dispatch' is present keyed to 6 files each containing the token, and _start_watch_producer maps to the four setattr sites I found by git grep. Held one point because the census counts (182 imports, 82 patches) rest on build_map.py's own scan, which check_map.py does not independently re-derive the census for beyond three named membership asserts; I spot-checked rather than exhaustively re-derived.
justifications.fit: The fragment follows the evidence-fragment template and carries the correct meta (docs-project reckon, reckon-type evidence, plan-evidence-for every-module-fits-a-worker-window, plan-verifies every-module-fits-a-worker-window#s3, plan-verdict mapped); the producer names describe concerns (dispatch_admission, dispatch_sessions) rather than part numbers, versions or the word 'core'; comments in build_map.py describe the mechanism (import-time expressions only, synthetic imports as an upper bound) with no plan label, ticket or attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The map's stated goal is fully met on independent verification. I recounted the base module's statements with my own ast walk (396, matching the JSON's placed_count), confirmed the multiset of members across the 11 modules is 396 unique names with no duplicate and no omission, confirmed the largest module (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py, 145 members) at 34,535 stored tokens against a 117,882-byte source with no module over 40,000, and confirmed zero module-level edges across all produced modules (88 function-level edges are recorded for the launch/session and plan clusters). The HTML fragment carries the module table, the seam account, the module-level-edge statement, the two back-references (dispatch_sessions.resume_plan/change_lane -> dispatch.FENCE_WORKERS) and the 70-path repoint list required by the brief. Held one point off for the plan/map count reconciliation above, which is a map-side omission (no cross-reference to §3's 320) rather than a defect in the placement.
justifications.reuse: The census half the plan insists on reuses the repository's importer index - build_map.py imports _import_targets from reckon.served_code rather than writing a second name scan - which is exactly §3's stated requirement. The checker re-derives placement and token estimates from the same AST the builder parsed. The only reuse cost is the literal math.ceil(bytes/3.5) standing in for reckon.crew.routing._tokens_for_bytes (numerically identical) and the builder being a run-directory script rather than a reusable helper probably belongs to the guard node.
justifications.scope_discipline: Perfect. git diff d01750d78..f55383af4 --name-status lists exactly the node's two declared write paths, both added; no code, test or script is touched; the node moved no code and renamed nothing under reckon/. Head is a clean descendant of base with no unrelated commits.
